interest: This file provides a revealing case study of how the Allied occupation regime navigated the complex boundary between wartime reparations and the revitalization of commercial export markets. It illuminates how prewar global trade networks—specifically the substantial pre-1941 export of Japanese and Korean leaf tobacco to Egyptian cigarette manufacturers—were swiftly mobilized by tenacious local commercial agents like Raphael Soussi, pushing SCAP and the State Department to establish trade mechanisms via the U.S. Commercial Company prior to the restoration of private foreign trade. Additionally, the collection documents SCAP's domestic economic stabilization strategies through SCAPIN 1854, showing how captured or surplus American tobacco products were systematically deployed as 'incentive goods' to spur critical coal extraction and official rice deliveries while guarding against black market diversion.
keywords: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP)
overview: This decimal file (894.61331) documents U.S. State Department and SCAP policies and commercial transactions concerning Japanese leaf tobacco from late 1945 through April 1949. The early correspondence centers on persistent efforts by Raphael S. Soussi, an Alexandria-based Egyptian import-export merchant and former agent of Nippon Menkwa Kabushiki Kaisha, to acquire accumulated stocks of Japanese, Korean, and Formosan leaf tobacco (notably Matsukawa type) initially framed as potential reparations payments and later structured as a commercial purchase via the U.S. Commercial Company (USCC) and SCAP. Later documents in the file shift to domestic occupation economic administration, featuring SCAP directive SCAPIN 1854 authorizing the Japanese Government to distribute American tobacco products as incentive goods to Japanese coal miners and rice farmers, as well as official SCAP statistical radiograms tracking postwar Japanese leaf tobacco trade and exports to Egypt and the United States between 1946 and 1949.

subfiles.about: The State Department instructs the American Consul General in Alexandria regarding the non-reparations status and official government channels required for acquiring Japanese tobacco stocks.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State transmits correspondence from Raphael S. Soussi forwarded by Ambassador Edwin W. Pauley concerning the acquisition of Japanese tobacco. The Department states that inquiries are underway in Japan to determine if tobacco stocks exist, noting that any tobacco would be treated as a commercial export rather than a reparations claim. Because private commercial transactions are not yet permitted with Japanese nationals, any purchase must be arranged through official accredited government channels, and Egyptian buyers are suggested to contact the British Mission in Tokyo.
subfiles.title: Instruction from Department of State to American Consul General in Alexandria on Japanese Tobacco Export Procedures

subfiles.about: H. D. Maxwell forwards correspondence from Raphael S. Soussi to Edward Martin at the State Department for official handling.
subfiles.from: H. D. Maxwell, Chief of Staff, Japanese Reparations Mission
subfiles.summary: H. D. Maxwell, Chief of Staff of Ambassador Pauley's Japanese Reparations Mission, transfers correspondence received from Raphael S. Soussi of Alexandria to Edward Martin of the State Department's economic division. Maxwell attaches a copy of his own reply of February 21 to Soussi along with Soussi's original letters. He notes that the enclosed materials regarding Japanese unmanufactured tobacco stocks are self-explanatory.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from H. D. Maxwell to Edward Martin Transmitting Soussi Correspondence
subfiles.to: Edward Martin, Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: H. D. Maxwell informs Raphael S. Soussi that inquiries regarding Japanese unmanufactured tobacco and reparations are handled by the State Department.
subfiles.from: H. D. Maxwell, Chief of Staff, Japanese Reparations Mission
subfiles.summary: Writing on behalf of Ambassador Pauley, H. D. Maxwell acknowledges Soussi's letters and telegrams regarding unmanufactured Japanese tobacco stocks. Maxwell explains that specific reparations details and commercial acquisition matters are handled directly by the Department of State in Washington rather than by the Pauley Mission. He advises Soussi to direct future communications to Edward Martin at the State Department and confirms that Soussi's correspondence has been referred to Martin.
subfiles.title: Letter from H. D. Maxwell to Raphael S. Soussi Referring Inquiries to State Department

subfiles.about: Justin R. Wolf acknowledges receipt of Raphael S. Soussi's initial letter during Ambassador Pauley's absence abroad.
subfiles.from: Justin R. Wolf, Office of Ambassador Edwin W. Pauley, The White House
subfiles.summary: Writing from the White House, Justin R. Wolf acknowledges receipt of Raphael S. Soussi's letter of November 10, 1945, addressed to Ambassador Edwin W. Pauley. Wolf notes that the letter arrived while Pauley was abroad on his reparations mission to the Far East. He assures Soussi that the letter and its enclosures will be forwarded immediately to Pauley.
subfiles.title: Letter from Justin R. Wolf to Raphael S. Soussi Acknowledging Correspondence to Pauley

subfiles.about: Raphael Soussi urgently cables Ambassador Pauley requesting prices, grades, and terms for purchasing Japanese tobacco as reparations.
subfiles.from: Raphael Soussi (cabled as Raphael Coussin), Alexandria, Egypt
subfiles.summary: Raphael Soussi cables Ambassador Edwin W. Pauley at the White House expressing keen urgency for a decision on Japanese tobacco supplies in payment of reparations. Soussi asserts that he has ready buyers in Egypt for whatever stocks are available or for future crop deliveries. He requests immediate notification of available qualities, grades, and price quotations on either an FOB Japan or CIF Egypt basis.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Raphael Soussi to Ambassador Edwin Pauley Inquiring on Japanese Tobacco Terms
subfiles.to: Ambassador Edwin Pauley, The White House, Washington

subfiles.about: Raphael S. Soussi follows up on his unanswered tobacco inquiries and asks the Secretary of State to refer his proposal to Major General Frank McCoy.
subfiles.summary: Soussi brings to the attention of the Secretary of State his unanswered communications addressed to Ambassador Pauley, enclosing a copy of his November 10, 1945 letter and citing his cable of January 30, 1946. Having learned that Major General Frank McCoy has replaced Pauley in Far Eastern reparations leadership, Soussi requests that his proposal be communicated to McCoy for a prompt response. He requests that the State Department take the necessary steps to provide a definite positive or negative answer to his application.
subfiles.title: Letter from Raphael S. Soussi to Secretary of State Requesting Action on Tobacco Application

subfiles.about: Raphael S. Soussi details the historical prewar trade in Japanese and Korean leaf tobacco to Egypt and proposes exporting surplus stocks in satisfaction of reparations.
subfiles.summary: Prompted by news reports of Ambassador Pauley's mission arriving in Tokyo, Soussi presents an extensive proposal for the export of Japanese, Korean, and Formosan leaf tobacco to Egypt as reparations. He explains that between 1918 and 1941 Egypt imported up to 4,000,000 pounds of Japanese and Korean tobacco annually for cigarette manufacture, representing roughly one-third of Egypt's total leaf imports, with prewar values of one to two million dollars and current values estimated at over ten million dollars. He lists specific accumulated tobacco types (including Matsukawa, Bitchu, Bingo, Daruma, Satsuma, Nambu, Korean, and Formosan varieties) and outlines flexible payment options in sterling, dollars, or Egyptian currency through the American Embassy. To substantiate his expertise, he provides commercial contacts at Kyodo Tobacco Company, Nippon Menkwa Kabushiki Kaisha, and the Japanese Tobacco Monopoly Bureau, alongside banking and diplomatic references in Cairo and Alexandria.
subfiles.title: Letter from Raphael S. Soussi to Edwin Pauley Proposing Purchase of Japanese and Korean Leaf Tobacco
subfiles.to: Edwin W. Pauley, Head of Far Eastern (Japan) Reparations Commission, Department of State

subfiles.about: The State Department informs the Consul General in Alexandria that inquiries have been directed to SCAP and that Soussi's U.S. representative has been briefed.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State transmits a copy of Raphael Soussi's letter of March 19, 1946, to the American Consul General in Alexandria for background information. The instruction advises that formal inquiries regarding the availability of exportable leaf tobacco stocks have been sent to SCAP Headquarters in Tokyo and that results will be communicated to Soussi once received. It further notes that the Department has been in contact with A. N. Thompson, the attorney representing Soussi's firm in the United States, keeping him appraised of the matter's status.
subfiles.title: Instruction from Department of State to American Consul General in Alexandria on Status of Tobacco Inquiries

subfiles.about: Raphael S. Soussi urges Edward Martin for a prompt decision on Japanese tobacco stocks and requests travel authorization to Tokyo to inspect leaf grades.
subfiles.summary: Writing to Edward Martin following H. D. Maxwell's referral, Soussi emphasizes the urgency of securing a definitive decision regarding exportable Japanese, Korean, and Formosan tobacco leaf stocks. He informs Martin that he has authorized attorney A. N. Thompson of RCA in San Francisco to negotiate directly with reparations and State Department officials in Washington. Soussi offers to travel personally to Washington or Tokyo to inspect and grade the tobacco, requesting that the State Department facilitate priority air passage on American carriers such as TWA at his own expense.
subfiles.title: Letter from Raphael S. Soussi to Edward Martin Urging Tobacco Allocation and Offering Tokyo Inspection
subfiles.to: Edward Martin, Division of Commercial Policy, Department of State

subfiles.about: The State Department instructs the American Consul in Alexandria to solicit a firm dollar bid from Raphael Soussi for 300 metric tons of Matsukawa tobacco.
subfiles.summary: The Department of State instructs the American Consul in Alexandria to obtain a firm purchase bid in U.S. dollars from Raphael Soussi for 300 metric tons of Matsukawa type leaf tobacco available for immediate export from Japan. The Consul is informed that an acceptable offer is estimated at $525 to $550 per ton f.o.b. Japan for typical grades. If an acceptable bid is secured, Soussi must establish an irrevocable letter of credit payable to the U.S. Secretary of the Treasury for SCAP, with physical shipping and handling anticipated through the U.S. Commercial Company.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Department of State to American Consul in Alexandria Requesting Soussi's Bid on Matsukawa Tobacco

subfiles.about: Consul Hooker A. Doolittle transmits Raphael Soussi's firm bid of $537.50 per metric ton for 300 metric tons of Matsukawa leaf tobacco.
subfiles.from: Hooker A. Doolittle, American Consul, Alexandria, Egypt
subfiles.summary: Consul Doolittle conveys Raphael Soussi's formal firm bid for 300 metric tons of 1944 or 1945 crop Matsukawa leaf tobacco across grades four, five, six, and seven (75 tons each) at an average price of $537.50 per ton f.o.b. Japan, including packing. The bid specifies Japanese Government quality certification, packaging in 50-kilo iron-hooped and straw-lined hessian bales, and requires either airmailed hand samples or an advance shipment of 500 bales before confirming the balance. Soussi conditions the purchase on Egyptian import licensing and dollar allocations, indicates readiness to negotiate for an additional 1,000 tons within six months, and requests priority air passage to Tokyo to inspect the leaf.
subfiles.title: Telegram from American Consul in Alexandria (Doolittle) Transmitting Raphael Soussi's Tobacco Bid

subfiles.about: The State Department informs the Consul in Alexandria that the U.S. Commercial Company will assume direct responsibility for the Japanese tobacco transaction.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledging Alexandria's telegrams 55 and 64, the State Department commends the consulate's prompt action in securing Soussi's bid. The message explains that the U.S. Commercial Company (USCC) is about to assume contractual responsibility for managing Japanese export transactions to third countries. Consequently, USCC will take over the direct initiative for advancing negotiations with Soussi, including the dispatch of airmailed tobacco leaf samples.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Department of State to American Consul in Alexandria Designating USCC to Handle Tobacco Transaction

subfiles.about: Consul Doolittle inquires about the State Department's decision on Soussi's bid to facilitate Egyptian import and currency approvals.
subfiles.from: Hooker A. Doolittle, American Consul, Alexandria, Egypt
subfiles.summary: Consul Doolittle cables Washington referring to his previous telegram 55 and the Department's telegram 38 concerning Soussi's bid. He reports that Soussi has formally submitted applications to the Egyptian Government for dollar exchange and an import permit. Doolittle requests an expedited decision from Washington, noting that official confirmation of the sale is urgently needed to secure Egyptian approval.
subfiles.title: Telegram from American Consul in Alexandria (Doolittle) Requesting Decision on Soussi Bid

subfiles.about: USPOLAD Tokyo transmits SCAP directive SCAPIN 1854 authorizing the release of American tobacco as incentive goods in Japan.
subfiles.from: Office of the United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo (Acting Political Adviser)
subfiles.summary: The Acting Political Adviser for Japan in Tokyo forwards to the Secretary of State five copies of SCAPIN 1854, dated January 30, 1948. The enclosed directive authorizes the Japanese Government to distribute designated quantities of American tobacco products in its custody as incentive goods. These goods are specifically designated to stimulate increased production among Japanese coal miners and to encourage rice deliveries to the official collection system.
subfiles.title: Despatch from USPOLAD Tokyo Transmitting SCAP Directive on Incentive Tobacco Distribution

subfiles.about: SCAP directive SCAPIN 1854 authorizes the Japanese Government to distribute American tobacco products as incentive goods to miners and farmers under strict controls.
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP)
subfiles.summary: Issued by Adjutant General Colonel R. M. Levy on behalf of General MacArthur, SCAPIN 1854 grants authority to the Japanese Government to release American tobacco products in its custody as incentive goods. The directive authorizes cigarette distribution to encourage coal extraction and rice delivery quotas, releases 250,000 packages of pipe tobacco to coal miners, allows 1,000 pounds of pipe tobacco and cigars for cigarette manufacturing tests, and releases chewing tobacco for farm insecticide production. It strictly mandates that all packages be distinctively marked to differentiate them from occupation force supplies, requires distribution solely through official channels to prevent illicit sales, and demands prior SCAP approval of pricing and distribution schedules.
subfiles.title: SCAP Directive SCAPIN 1854 Authorizing Distribution of American Tobacco as Incentive Goods
subfiles.to: Japanese Government (through Central Liaison Office, Tokyo)

subfiles.about: SCAP Tokyo reports leaf tobacco trade figures for 1946-1947 and projects exports of 10,000 metric tons to Egypt in 1948.
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP), Tokyo
subfiles.summary: In response to a joint inquiry from the State Department and Department of the Army, SCAP Tokyo transmits a statistical summary of Japanese leaf tobacco trade. The report states that calendar year 1946 saw zero imports and zero exports, while calendar year 1947 saw zero imports and 492 metric tons of leaf tobacco exported to Egypt. SCAP further forecasts that leaf tobacco exports during calendar year 1948 will total approximately 10,000 metric tons, identifying Egypt as the primary prospective market.
subfiles.title: Telegram from SCAP Tokyo Reporting 1946-1947 Tobacco Trade Statistics and 1948 Export Forecast
subfiles.to: Secretary of State and Department of the Army

subfiles.about: SCAP transmits updated leaf tobacco statistics for 1947-1948 and outlines detailed crop export estimates for 1949.
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP), Tokyo
subfiles.summary: SCAP reports revised leaf tobacco trade data to the Department of the Army for transmission to the State Department. The report reconfirms 1947 figures of zero imports and 492 metric tons exported to Egypt, and notes that 1948 imports were zero while 3.2 metric tons were exported to the United States. For calendar year 1949, projected exports total 850 metric tons of 1947 crop sun-cured, 2,500 metric tons of 1948 crop sun-cured, and 1,500 metric tons of 1948 crop flue-cured tobacco, with zero imports anticipated.
subfiles.title: Telegram from SCAP Tokyo Reporting Leaf Tobacco Trade Figures and 1949 Export Forecast
subfiles.to: Department of the Army and Secretary of State
